File sessions¶

A file session keeps the state of the file viewer in a small file, so that you can go back to the same work later. When you open the session, wvt opens the recording and shows it as it was.

A session file keeps these items:

Item

Contents

The recording

Its path, the sample format, the header, I/Q swap, the sample rate, the center frequency and the segment

The view

The time span, the frequency span and relative frequency

The waterfall

The FFT size, the window, the overlap, the averages, the size limits, the dB range, Auto, the colormap and peak hold

The layout

The panel sizes, the overview strip, and which time plots show and fit their Y axis

The channel

On or off, the offset, the bandwidth, the taps, the decimation, and the AM, FM and PM settings and the squelch

Markers and bookmarks

The time and frequency markers, the point markers (P1 and P2), and all the bookmarks

A session does not keep the live mode, the signal generator, the audio window or the export window.

Save a session¶

  1. Open a recording, and set the view and the plots as you want them.

  2. Select File → Save File Session….

  3. Make sure that the path is correct. The default is the name of the recording with .wvtsession.json, in the folder of the recording.

  4. Click Save.

wvt does not replace an existing file. To replace it, tick Replace an existing file.

From the command line, --session-out F opens the recording with the other options, writes the session to F, then stops:

wvt cap.sigmf-meta --view 10:10.5 --chan 300k:150k --session-out cap.wvtsession.json

Open a session¶

Type the path of the session file in the File box and press Enter, or give it on the command line:

wvt cap.wvtsession.json

wvt looks at the contents of the file, not only its name: a session file is a small JSON file with a wvt_session member. Thus a recording (for example a .bin file) or SigMF metadata is never opened as a session.

The session keeps the path of the recording in two forms: the full path, and the path from the folder of the session file. wvt tries the second form first. Thus, if you move a folder that has the recording and its session, the session still finds the recording.

The file format¶

The session file is JSON. You can read and change it with a text editor. Part of a session file (... shows where members are left out here):

{
  "wvt_session": 1,
  "recording": {"path": "/data/cap.sigmf-data", "relative_path": "cap.sigmf-data", "datatype": "ci16_le",
                "header_bytes": 0, "swap_iq": false, "sample_rate": 2400000, "center_freq": 100000000,
                "segment_s": [-1, -1]},
  "view": {"t0_s": 10, "t1_s": 10.5, "f0_hz": 98800000, "f1_hz": 101200000, "relative_freq": false},
  "waterfall": {"nfft": 1024, "window": "Blackman-Harris", "overlap_pct": 50, ...},
  "layout": {...},
  "channel": {"enabled": true, "offset_hz": 300000, "bandwidth_hz": 150000, ...},
  "markers": {...},
  "points": {"shown": true, "p1": {"plot": "am", "t_s": 10.12}, "p2": {"plot": "waterfall", "t_s": 10.15, "f_hz": 100300000}},
  "bookmarks": [{"name": "burst", "t0_s": 10.1, "t1_s": 10.2}]
}

  • segment_s -1 is the start or the end of the file.

  • plot of a point marker is waterfall, spectrum, i, q, am, fm or pm. A marker on the waterfall has t_s and f_hz, on the spectrum f_hz, and on a time plot t_s.

  • A member that is not in the file gets its default value. Only recording is necessary.

  • A session file from a newer wvt (a larger wvt_session number) is refused.
